title: I directed AI agents to build a complete Unreal Engine 5.9 game in 4 days — here's the workflow and result
author: No-Mixture-9814
selftext:
I just released The Unmade, a free gothic puzzle adventure built for the Epic AI MegaJam 2026.

Game: https://vovozera.itch.io/theunmade

The challenge was to produce a playable Unreal Engine 5.9 game using an AI-driven workflow, with one human developer responsible for creative and technical direction.

Our production pipeline:

\- GPT-6 / ChatGPT: Narrative, GDD, technical specifications, feature planning, and agent coordination.

\- OpenAI Codex: Unreal C++, gameplay systems, GAS, persistence, and automated testing.

\- Claude + Unreal MCP: Blueprints, world integration, UI, animation, VFX, and cinematics.

\- Gemini / Antigravity: Visual and technical production, architecture, and animation workflows.

\- Blender / Tripo: 3D asset production and integration.

What worked:

Separating native gameplay authority from Blueprint presentation helped us integrate multiple AI-generated systems without constantly replacing existing functionality.

The project uses Gameplay Ability System, World Partition, UMG/MVVM, Enhanced Input, and Unreal Gameplay Cameras.

What didn't work initially:

We encountered camera integration problems, animation import scale errors, material inconsistencies, and UI layout issues.

These required real debugging, corrections, and Editor validation.

The biggest lesson:

AI can generate a significant amount of content, but integration, consistency, debugging, and direction remain essential.

The game's core mechanic reflects this philosophy: you sacrifice parts of yourself to restore a broken world.

The game is free for Windows, and the development process is documented in our Glass Box Devlog on itch.io.

I'd be interested in comparing workflows with other developers using Unreal Engine and AI agents.
